Team — forwarding ACME's note and the attached redline. Key asks: unlimited indemnity for third-party IP claims outside the cap, and removal of consequential-damages exclusion for IP. ACME wants fast turnaround; they aim to sign next week.

Context / constraints: we generally push for IP indemnities tied to our code/model deliverables and require the customer to provide prompt notice and control of defense. We also try to avoid open-ended indemnity exposure to downstream usage or customer-supplied prompts.

Questions for legal (Marissa):
- Can we draft a narrow carve-out that makes the indemnity for third-party IP infringement "outside the liability cap" but limited to claims arising from Redwood-owned model code or prepackaged model weights (i.e., not customer uploads or fine-tunes)?
- If the indemnity is outside the cap, should we still try to limit remedies to actual costs plus replacement/repair and require mitigation steps (e.g., cease-use clause) rather than open-ended statutory damages?
- Would an insurance/escrow requirement be a reasonable compromise for the customer?

NAOMI: if you can confirm whether ACME expects subcontractor coverage that would help shape language.

Thanks — need your recommended redline to respond to ACME this afternoon.

Jonas

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com, naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-11-15T12:14:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Order Form / MSA - liability carve-outs for IP claim (ACME redlines)

Jonas / Naomi —

Appreciate the heads-up. Below is a recommended approach that balances ACME's commercial need and Redwood's risk model. High-level summary first, then proposed contract language.

Summary recommendation (short):
- We can offer a narrowly drawn carve-out that treats Redwood's indemnity for third-party IP infringement as "outside the liability cap" but only for claims that: (i) directly allege infringement by Redwood's prepackaged models, model weights, or Redwood-delivered code; and (ii) do not arise from Customer-provided data, Customer fine-tuning, or Customer modifications.
- Remedies for an IP determination should be limited to costs of defense, settlement amounts, and either (A) replacement/repair of the infringing component or (B) a reasonable monetary award reflecting direct damages; consequential or punitive damages remain excluded.
- We should include: (1) express notice and cooperation obligations; (2) Redwood's right to control defense and settle; and (3) a carve-out that extends to Redwood's subcontractors only where Redwood has contractual flow-down obligations and the subcontractor's conduct is within Redwood's control.
- As a commercial compromise, propose a per-claim cap for non-monetary relief (e.g., injunctive remedies) limited to USD 5,000,000 and require ACME to maintain commercially reasonable insurance. If ACME insists on no cap for monetary IP indemnity, request a reciprocal representation that ACME will allow Redwood to remediate/replace prior to monetary damages.

Proposed redline excerpt (editable):
"Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Parties agree that (a) Redwood's indemnification obligations with respect to third-party claims alleging that the Service or Redwood-delivered software or model weights infringe a third party's intellectual property rights shall not be subject to the Liability Cap set forth in Section [X], provided that such claim does not arise from Customer Data, Customer provided models or fine-tuning, or Customer modifications; and (b) damages recoverable in connection with such infringement shall be limited to reasonable costs of defense, settlement amounts, and either (i) replacement or modification of the infringing component to avoid infringement, or (ii) a monetary award reflecting direct damages. Consequential, special, punitive or indirect damages are excluded. Redwood shall have the right to assume and conduct the defense, subject to Customer's reasonable cooperation, and to seek recovery from any applicable subcontractor to the extent Redwood has flow-down rights."

Recommended process items:
- Attach this as a tracked redline to the MSA and propose a short call (15–20m) to confirm scope and subcontractor coverage.
- If ACME needs stronger recourse for injunctive risk, offer the USD 5M per-claim cap as the maximum injunctive/relief exposure.
- If ACME refuses any form of limit, escalate for exec approval and consider an insurance-first path (we ask ACME to carry specified EPL/IP insurance and Redwood provides evidence).

I attached a clean PDF with the redline and the excerpt above (proposed-ip-carveout-draft.pdf). If you want, I can send directly to ACME with Naomi copied.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Transactions
Redwood Inference

Evan —

Thanks for the clear note. We've reviewed and propose the following compromise for inclusion in the MSA (attached as a tracked change in redlined_orderform_jonas_20261115.docx):

- A narrowly tailored carve-out: Redwood's IP indemnity for third-party claims alleging infringement by Redwood-delivered models, model weights, or Redwood software will be outside the general Liability Cap, provided the claim does not arise from Customer Data, Customer-supplied models, or Customer-induced fine-tuning or modifications.
- Recoverable remedies shall be limited to costs of defense, settlement amounts, and either replacement/repair of the infringing component or a monetary award for direct damages. Consequential, punitive and indirect damages remain excluded.
- Redwood shall have the right to assume and conduct the defense, subject to Customer cooperation; Redwood will flow down obligations to subcontractors where contractually possible.
- As a commercial compromise on injunctive risk, Redwood proposes a USD 5,000,000 per-claim cap on non-monetary injunctive/relief exposures.

We attached the proposed language and a short rationale. If that looks ok to ACME, we'll issue an updated MSA and a DocuSign request (link below) for execution. If ACME needs a higher injunctive cap or unconditional unlimited indemnity for all IP scenarios, we'll need to escalate to execs for approval.
